Privacy Policy

Kenneth and Catherine run this site for their wedding on Saturday, 12 December 2026 at Edgie's Restaurant and Events in Marikina. Here is what it knows about you, in plain words.

Last updated 22 October 2026

What you give us

The RSVP card asks for five things only: your full name, your email address, whether you can come, whether you are bringing a guest, and that guest's name if you say yes. Nothing else is required. There is no field for a phone number, a home address, a payment detail or a dietary note.

What happens to it

Your answer is saved to one small private database that belongs to this site, so the couple can count seats and prepare a guest list. It is not sold, not rented, not advertised to, and not added to any mailing list. Only Kenneth and Catherine, and the few people they personally ask to help with the seating, read it.

What the site leaves on your device

This site does not plant advertising or tracking cookies of its own. The music player writes one small note into your browser's local storage so that two open tabs of the same song do not play over each other. Clearing your browser storage removes it.

Third-party code we cannot switch off

The site was built with a website platform, and every page still loads files from its servers, mainly static.parastorage.com and use.typekit.net. When you open a page, the platform records ordinary technical details such as your device type, browser, screen size and the page you came from, sends error and performance reports to services like frog.wix.com, panorama.wixapps.net and browser.sentry-cdn.com, and its own scripts may set cookies. That data is governed by the platform's privacy notice, not ours, and we cannot turn it off without the pages breaking.

How long we keep it

RSVP answers stay with the couple until they are finished with the guest list. Nothing on this site deletes them automatically before then.

Your choices

There is no self-service delete button here. If you would like a copy of what you sent us, or want it removed, tell Kenneth or Catherine, or pass the word to a principal sponsor or any member of the wedding party. We will do it, and we will confirm it back to you.

Accessibility Statement

We want every guest to be able to read the details, answer the questions and send us an RSVP, whatever device they use and however they browse.

Checked 22 October 2026

The standard we aim for

The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, WCAG 2.1, at Level AA.

What we have checked ourselves

  • Every page is marked as English, so a screen reader pronounces it correctly.
  • Words are deep red on beige or cream. We measured the body text at 5.6 to 1 contrast or better, and the larger headings higher again.
  • Nothing is carried by colour alone: the dress-code swatches name their colours, and the play, pause and mute icons each have a text label.
  • The pictures have alternative text, and artwork that is only decoration is marked as decoration.
  • The menu, the FAQ questions, the RSVP form and cards like this one work with the keyboard alone. Tab moves, Enter or Space activates, Escape closes. This card keeps the keyboard inside itself while it is open and hands it back where you came from.
  • The layout falls into a single column on a phone, and enlarging the text does not hide any of it.
  • If your device asks for reduced motion, the smooth scrolling and the animated intro are switched off.

What is not perfect yet

  • On the published site the song can begin by itself the first time a page is opened. Browser rules make it start silently until you touch something, and one press on the record stops it, but we know unexpected sound is not welcome for everyone.
  • Some of the page structure comes from the website platform rather than from us, such as its top-of-page and bottom-of-page regions, so we cannot promise that every part reads the way we would write it from scratch.
  • The site has not been assessed by an outside accessibility auditor. These checks were made by the people who built it, on a desktop browser and on a phone.

Tell us if something blocks you

Say so to Kenneth or Catherine, or to a principal sponsor or any member of the wedding party. We will fix it, or send you the same information another way, by text, by phone call, or on a printed card, whichever suits you.
